table.title: Strikes in July, 1928
table.caption_extra: Shanghai Strikes in 1928 — The following is a summary of strikes during the month of July.*

rows: Toa Seima Kaisha Ltd., 64 Robinson Road, Shanghai
Refusal on the part of the management to grant workers' demand for reduced working hours and higher pay.

(1) That work be stopped an hour earlier every day at 4.30 p.m. instead of 5 :30 p.m. (2) That at the end of every month extra pay equivalent to four instead of two days' wages be given to each worker. (3) That wages be paid on pay day as usual in case of a worker's record book having been lost.
(1) One more day's extra pay every month, or, a total of three days' extra pay. (2) Payment of wages as usual to any worker who has lost his record book, if he is guaranteed by the foreman.
Employees of Bean Curd Shops at Chang Chia Hang, Hu Chia Mu Chiao, Li Hung Kou, and Paoshing Road, Chapei, Shanghai.
Yin Feng Silk Filature, Tan Chia Chiao, Chapei, Shanghai

Hung Lung Waste Cocoon Factory, Kung Hsing Chiao, Chapei, Liu Ying Road, Shanghai, Ta Lun Waste Cocoon Factory, Tan Chia Chiao, Chapei, Shanghai, and Ching Lun Waste Cocoon Factory, Tientungan Road, Chapei, Shanghai
360 women employed by Hung Lun, 240 by Ta Lun, and 250 by Ching Lun, totalling 850.
Nagai Wata Kaisha Mill No. 9, 60 Markham Road, Shanghai
17 days (July 11-15 inclusive—5 days, July 18-21 inclusive—4 days, and July 24-31 inclusive—8 days, totalling 17 days).
Increase of working hours by ½ hour from 11 to 11½ hours per day.
That the old time schedule be resumed.
½ hour increase in working hours with 3 cents extra pay and a certain amount of retirement grant to be given to each of the workers dismissed, on account of the strike.
Assistants at Peanut Shops and Candy Shops in Shanghai, with labour union at Kung Ch'ing Fang, Kao Teng Chieh, Native City, Shanghai
Failure on the part of the managements to grant the assistants' demands for higher wages, better working conditions, and reinstatement of dismissed workers.

(1) Recognition of the representative right of the workers' union. (2) No dismissal of any worker without good cause, and, in case of dismissal, the approval of the labour union necessary; no employment of non-union members. (Any non-union member already in employment should voluntarily resign within ten days after the new agreement shall have come into force, leaving his position to be filled by a union member). (3) $10 increase for workers receiving $5 or less per month; $7 increase for those receiving $10 or less, $6 increase for those receiving $15 or less, and $5 increase for those receiving $20 or less. (4) Increase of monthly subsidy from $1 to $2. (5) A monthly allowance of $2 to each apprentice during the first year of apprenticeship, $3 during the second year, and $4 during the third year, and a minimum wage of $8 per month after apprenticeship. (6) Three-tenths of the annual net profit to be distributed among employees, including apprentices and coolies, as bonus. (7) (a) Double salaries for the 6th moon and 12th moon every year. (b) 60 days' leave of absence obtainable every year. (c) $1,000 compensation to anv worker who is killed by accident or incapacitated for life through injuries sustained while on duty. (8) Medical expenses in case of sickness to be borne by the managements. (9) (a) 12 working hours per day at most. (b) Holidays on festival days and general holidays, with full pay for those who do not work on holidays and double pay for those who work. (10) Apprentices to be sent by the management to night schools. (11) When eating no more than 7 persons shall sit at one table, and the diet shall consist of two kinds of animal food, two of vegetable food, and one of soup. (12) Abolition of the old rules forbidding employees to be absent during the busy months of 11th moon and 12th moon, to resign during these two months, or to ask for pay before pay day during any month of the year. (13) Retention of the old privileges enjoyed by the employees. (14) Compensation of any loss to the employees due to burglary, robbery, or fire.

table.title: Strikes in August, 1928
table.caption_extra: Shanghai Strikes in 1928 — The following is a summary of strikes during the month of August :†

rows: Employees of Chinese Drug Stores and Medicine Shops in Greater Shanghai, with a union at Yao Huang Miao, Yao Chu Lung, Native City, and a business office at 875 Hung Hsing Li, Peking Road.
3,500 employed by 215 shops, 196 in Greater Shanghai, 12 in Pootung, and 7 in Woosung.
Refusal of the employers to meet certain demands submitted by the employees.
(1) Increase in wages. (2) Better treatment. (3) Reinstatement of the workers recently dismissed.

The following conditions were ageed upon :— (1) Recognition of the representative right of the employees' union. (2) Employment of union members first. (3) (a) No dismissal of workers without cause. (b) No dismissal of workers participating in union activities if the employers are duly notified beforehand. (c) Not more than two-tenths of the workers of a shop to attend an ordinary meeting of the union with a grant of 4 hours' leave of absence. (d) Observance of general holidays with full pay or double pay for employees who work on these days. (e) 12 hours' working hours per day which may be prolonged to 13 on the 1st and 15th days of every month of both the lunar and Gregorian calendars. (f) Workers free to leave the shops after closing time. (g) Co-operation with the old workers in engaging additional workers. (h) Employment of union-members as substitutes in cases where any of the druggists will be absent from duties for more than 10 days in succession. (i) 2 months' leave of absence with full pay obtainable every year and double pay for those who do not make use of this privilege. (j) 30 hours' absence from work permissible every month and enforcement of reduction on wages on the basis of 12 hours as a whole day in case of worker being absent more than 30 hours during a month. (k) 1 month's leave for workers from other districts, and 1/2 months's leave for native workers obtainable on occasion of a wedding or funeral. (l) Medical expenses in case of sickness to be borne by the employers, besides full pay during the period of sickness, and proper care of tuberculosis workers in any designated hospital for not more than three months with the employers responsible for all the expenses incurred. (m) Payment of bonus due him in case of a worker resigning for a better position. (n) Payment of compensation equivalent to 1 to 2 years's wages to any worker killed by accident while on duty. (4) Appropriate increases in wages. (5) (a) Only 2 apprentices to be admitted every year by a shop of the best class, 1 by a shop of either the 1st, 2nd or 3rd class, and 1 in every 2 years by a shop of the 4th class. (b) No work outside of the shop to be given to apprentices. (c) No maltreatment of apprentices. (6) (a) Fair distribution of commission money among the employees without discount. (b) A monthly subsidy of $1 to every worker. (7) Three-thirteenths of any annual net profit to be divided among the employees as bonus. (8) The food per table to include 3 kinds of animal food and 2 kinds of vegetables. (9) Establishment of a business office at the union address. (10) Subsidy to the free school maintained by the employees.
Butchers in Tsao Chia Tu Village, Shanghai, with a union at 837 Jessfield Road, Tsao Chia Tu,
Silk Filatures North of the Soochow Creek, Shanghai, (上海北區絲廠).
Refusal on the part of the managements to grant the workers demand for shorter working hours on account of the hot weather.
(1) Working hours per day from 6 A.M. to 5.30 P.M. (2) Full pay during the period of strike.
(1) Working hours to be from 6 A.M. to 5.45 P.M. during the hot season. (2) Question of wages during the period of strike to be considered later.
Second Class Silk and Satin Shop Employees' Union, 4 Yu Li, Kwangsi Road Shanghai.

Arrest of the union members by the police following a quarrel between some union members and the owner of the San I Silk and Satin Shop, Corner of Nanking and Fukien Roads, who was said to have violated the time schedule decided upon between the employees and the employers on August 2 by opening his shop earlier than 9 o'clock in the morning.

(1) Enforcement of the agreement signed on August 2. (2) Release of the employees arrested. (3) Due compensation to injured workers for medical expenses and other losses. (4) Formal apology from the employers to be published in newspapers. (5) Punishment of the owner of the San I Shop. (6) Guarantee that no similar occurrence should arise in the future.

A. Payment of $300 by the owner of the San I Shop as compensation to the employees' union. B. The old agreement was revised as follows :— (1) The employees' union shall be recognized as the workers' sole representative. (2) No workers shall be dismissed without cause and the employment of union members shall be considered first when engaging additional workers. (3) A committee composed of three representatives from the employees shall be formed to study and promote the welfare of the employees, any expenses to be incurred to be borne by the employers. (4) The number of working hours per day shall be 10 from 9 A.M. to 7 P.M. (5) Wages shall be increased as follows :—$5 increase each for the workers receiving within $5 a month; $4 increase for those receiving within $10 a month; $3 increase for those receiving from $11 to $20 a month; $2 increase for those receiving from $21 to $30 a month; and $1 increase for those receiving more than $30 a month. Wages shall be increased once a year, the minimum increase being $2 per month. Wages shall be doubled for the 5th, 8th, and 12th moons of the lunar year. A uniform monthly subsidy of $1 each shall be paid to all the apprentices, coolies, and other employees. (6) A monthly allowance of $2 shall be granted to each apprentice in the first year of apprenticeship, $3 for the second year, and $5 for the third year, at the end of which period the apprentice shall receive at least $10 per month as wages. Appropriate education shall be accorded free to all the apprentices. (7) The annual net profits shall be divided into 13 equal shares for appropriation, three of these shares to be distributed among the employees as bonus. (8) Each worker shall be entitled to a total 70 days' leave of absence every year with full pay. Full pay shall be issued in case of sickness and the medical expenses shall be borne by the employers. Full pay shall be given to any worker who absents himself from work in order to join certain activities of the union, but the total number of workers in a shop who do so at the same time shall not exceed three. One month's leave with full pay shall be accorded to any worker on occasion of a wedding or funeral. (9) Appropriate compensation shall be given to the family of any worker incapacitated for life or who died from injuries sustained while doing some service for the employers. (10) Equal treatment shall be extended to all the employees regardless of their status in the shops. (11) In cases of dismissial of workers and suspension of business due to bankruptcy or otherwise, the matters shall be adjusted according to the labour laws to be promulgated by the Nationalist Government. (12) The shop accountants shall help to collect the monthly membership dues to the workers' union from the workers. (13) The agreement shall take effect from the date of its execution.
Toa Seima Kaisha, Robinson Road, Shanghai.
Refusal on the part of the management to increase the bonus paid to the workers according to their speed of production and the quality of the goods produced.
An increase will be given on account of extra good work.
Public Ricksha Coolies who hire their rickshas from the ricksha hong in Jui Kang Li, East Kashing Road, Shanghai.
Attempt of the ricksha hong to exact 24 instead of 23 coppers as a dime from the coolies when collecting the hire fees.
That 23 coppers only be considered equivalent to 1 dime.
China Merchants Tobacco Co., 69 Ward Road, Shanghai.
Intention on the part of the management to shift certain workers in the package packing department to the tin packing department owing to business depression.
That the workers be allowed to remain in the package packing department.
China Navigation Pootung Wharf Labour Union, Tien Tang Lung, Pootung :
Assistants at Peanut and Candy Shops in Shanghai (whose labour union has been removed to 882 Hung Hsing Li, Peking Road. (Cf. Summary of Strikes for July).
The case was handed over to the Chinese municipal authorities for arbitration.
Hwa Ching Tobacco Co., Ltd., 281-2 Yunnan Road, Shanghai.
40 employed by No. 3 Factory at 30 Dixwell Road, (狄思威路三十號) and 280 employed by the new factory at Wayside Road (匯山路), totalling 320.

table.title: Strikes in September, 1928
table.caption_extra: Shanghai Strikes in 1928 — The following is a summary of strikes during the month of September :*

rows: Incense Employees' Union, Dai Chi Road, Nantao, Shanghai.
Non-compliance on the part of the managements with the workers' demands for wage increases and better treatment.

(1) Recognition of the representative right of the employees' union. (2) No deduction of wages of those who absent themselves from work with notification to the management on account of urgent business in connection with the union. (3) No dismissal without good reason and the approval of the union. (4) No employment of non-members of the union. (5) Employment or dismissal with the approval of the union once a year during the Dragon Boat Festival only. (6) A subsidy to the union of $1.00 per month from each employer. (7) 40 per cent increase in wages for workers working in the workshop, and payment of rewards in "big money" with 50 per cent increase, (Mammon Festival, $0.40; Ching Ming Festival, $0.30; Dragon Boat Festival, $0.40; Mid-September, $0.30 : Mid-Autumn, $0.55; First day of the tenth moon, $0.30; Chinese New Year, $1.60; 15th day of the 1st moon, $0.30; Beginning of summer, $0.20; Beginning of autumn, $0.15; 9th day of the 9th moon, $0.30; Winter Solstice, $0.30.) (8) 8 hours of work per day, and night shift from mid-July to mid-August. (9) Observation of 1st and 15th each moon as holidays with full pay. (10) Payment of 15 months' wages per year; 1 month's leave of absence with full pay; daily deduction in wages in case of more than 1 month's absence; and exception in case of emergency. (11) $3.00 increase in wages; $0.10 per 100 Ku for those binding San Hsin Incense; $0.20 per 100 Ku for those binding Wan Shue Increase; and $1.00 monthly fee for both employees and apprentices. (12) Payment of all medical expenses of the employees by the employers and no wage deduction for any worker on sick leave. (13) Admission of 1 apprentice only per shop or per workshop, and next admission permissible only after the completion of the apprenticeship by the first admitted apprentice.

(1) Recognition of the representative right of the union. (2) No deduction of wages for absent workers with notification of the higher labour union. (3) No dismissal without the approval of the union. (4) No employment of non-members of the union. (5) Employment or dismissal of workers 3 times a year according to the old regulation. (6) $0.08 increase in wages (originally $0.40). (7) $0.002 per catty increase in wages (originally $0.013 per catty) for the grinder; $0.20 increase per basin for the mixer (originally $1.60 to $1.80 per basin); $0.004 increase per catty for the polisher and beater (originally $0.026 per catty); $0.001 increase per catty for the waste worker. (8) Working hours for the packers from morning till 5 :00 p.m., overtime from 6 :00 p.m. to 10 :30 p.m., during the period from mid-July to mid-August and the month of December. (9) No packing work on the 1st and 15th of each moon. (10) Payment of wages in 14 moons and 24 days, and deduction in wages in case of absence for more than one month. (11) $1.50 increase in wages for shop employees; 20 per cent increase for workshop employees; and a monthly subsidy of 10 dimes (originally 6 dimes) for each employee as well as apprentice.
Hua Yang Printers' Union, 8 Paoshan Road, Shanghai.
The dismissal of 31 workers of the Shun Lee & Co., Ltd., B 60 Kiangsi Road, Shanghai, who refused to work on the night shift.

Reinstatement of the workers dismissed as the first step toward settlement. (1) Recognition of the representative right of the Printers' Union. (2) No employment of non-members of the union and dismissal of those who do not apply for the membership of the union, after fifteen days of the signing of the settlement. (3) Treatment : (a) Eight hours' work per day. (b) No dismissal without good reason and approval of the union. (c) The employed must be members of the union. (d) Sunday, Spring Festival, Dragon Boat Festival, Mid-Autumn Festival, Winter Festival and other days shall be observed as holidays, and in addition, holidays for the Chinese New Year and the Gregorian New Year shall be given according to the custom and the regulation of the Higher Labour Union. Full pay for holidays and double pay for working during holidays. (e) Payment of fractions of a dollar in 'big money.' (f) A monthly subsidy of $8.00 for boarding and $2.00 for lodging shall be given to each worker. Equal treatment shall be accorded to all employees including the apprentices. (g) Financial assistance to the union for educational purposes : $1.00 monthly from an employer whose employees are under the number of ten, $2.00 from an employer having under 20 employees, and due subsidy on the basis of $0.10 per worker from an employer employing more than 20 workers. (h) One month's furlough with pay to any workers from outports in case of a marriage or funeral and half a month's leave with pay for any local worker. (i) Payment of all medical expenses of workers by the employers and payment of two months' wages to workers on sick leave. (j) A compensation equivalent to two years' wages to any worker who died from injuries sustained while on duty. (k) A furlough of five to ten days with full pay for any worker in case of emergency, but such privileges are not available more than six times a year. (l) No deduction of wages of the workers who absent themselves from work to attend union meetings if notification is given beforehand to the employers. (m) One apprentice per year only to be admitted into a shop with more than thirty employees, one in a year and a half in case of a shop with 20 to 30 employees, one in two years in case of that with 10 to 20 employees, and one in three years in case of that with less than 10 employees. (n) An allowance of $24.00 to an apprentice for the first year, $36.00 for the second year and $48.00 for the third year. A minimum wage of $10.00 per month to those who have completed the three years of apprenticeship. (o) No work for the apprentices except that concerning the shop itself. (p) No heavy and dangerous work for apprentices. (4) Wages. (a) $6.00 increase for workers earning under $10.00 per month; $5.00 for those earning under $20.00; $4.00; for those earning under $30.00; $3.00 for those earning under $40.00; $2.00 for those earning under $50.00; $1.00 for those earning more than $50.00; and an increase in wages yearly. (b) Double pay at the beginning and end of every year. (c) A gratuity of 4 days' wages to those workers who have not been absent from work during all working hours during a whole month; one month's wages to those who have received such gratuity for one year. (d) No deduction of wages of those who are late within fifteen minutes in the morning. (e) Annual promulgation of the balanced account and bonus of 30% of net profit to the workers.
Rice Employees' Union, 430 Hui Wen Road, Chapei :
Non-compliance on the part of the employers with the worker's demands of November, 1927, for increase of wages and improvement in treatment.
Compliance with the demands of November, 1927.
Yung Hing Tai Silk Filature, Tien Tung An Road, Chapei.
160 women workers and 120 female juvenile workers.
Monks in Haichao Temple, 3 Lieuyun Road, Small South Gate, Nantao, Shanghai :
Automatic Hosiery Machine Manufacture Employees' Union, 2 Stone Street, Ching Lung Chiao, Nantao, Shanghai :
Non-compliance on the part of the management with the workers' demands for wage increases and better treatment.

(1) Recognition of the representative right of the union. (2) No dismissal without reasonable cause. (3) An 8-hour day. (4) An increase of $6 should be given to those earning under $10 per month: $4 to those earning between $10 and $20; $3 to those earning between $20 and $25; and $2 to those earning between $20 and $25; and $2 to those earning between $25 and $30.
Tsai Tung Teh Drug Store, Honan Road, Shanghai.
Fancy Paper Printing Trade, Fuyu Road, Native City, Shanghai.

table.title: Strikes in October, 1928
table.caption_extra: Shanghai Strikes in 1928 — The following is a summary of strikes during the month of October.*

rows: Hwa Ching Tobacco Co., Ltd., 68 Wayside Road.
Chih-ming Weaving and Dyeing Factory (weaving department), 347 Arsenal Road, Nantao, Shanghai.
General Post Office and 23 Branch Offices, Shanghai.
Failure on the part of the management to meet their employees' demands for wage increases and better treatment.

(1) That the wage system be revised throughout the country according to a uniform increase of 33.33 per cent in each successive rank, and Shanghai employees to be given an allowance, in addition. (2) That the Postal regulations be revised within a year and that representatives of the employees' union be admitted to the committee appointed to carry out the revision. (3) That the Postal Authorities permit the organization of a National Labour Union of all Postal employees, and allow $10,000 for its inauguration, and a subsidy of $500 monthly. (4) That the Postal authorities immediately release the sum granted to the Shanghai employees' union as its opening expenses and further increase it to $2,000 and also increase the monthly subsidy to $200. (5) That any employee is to be dismissed only with the consent of the union. (6) That the members of the standing committee of the Postal union be exempted from post office duties and be given the usual pay and promotion. (7) That the Postal authorities give $2,000 for the opening of a school for employees' children, and $200 per month thereafter for its maintenance. (8) That an adequate solatium be given to the family of a deceased employee. (9) That no limit be placed on sick leave, and, medical expenses be borne by the Post Office authorities. (10) That a New Year bonus of one month's pay be given to those having less than three years' service and a bonus of two months' pay to those having more than three years' service. (11) That all employees be entitled to rest on Sundays and holidays, but if given work on these days, earn extra pay. (12) That all employees be given equal treatment in matters pertaining to general holidays and long leave. (13) That the present system of promotion by class be abolished and a general promotion once a year be instituted in its place. (14) That an allowance of $3 per month be issued to courtyard coolies. (15) That the sum of $30 deducted from the death gratuity of a deceased employee named Shun Moh-tsun be refunded and an apology be tendered by the person responsible for the deduction. (16) That the deducted wages of employees engaged on draft desks be refunded and the person responsible for be given warning.
The above demands were handed by the local Kuomintang and the Municipality of Greater Shanghai to be transmitted to the Ministry of Communications for consideration and decision.
Automatic Hosiery Machine Manufacture Employees' Union, 2 Stone Street, Ching Lung Chiao, Nantao, Shanghai : (Cf. Summary of Strikes for September, 1928).

(1) Recognition of the representative rights of the Employees' Union. (2) Approval of the Employees' Union necessary in case of dismissal. (3) Increase of $1 for those earning more than $20 per month; $2 for those earning more than $10; and $3 for those earning under $10. (4) Working hours to be reduced to 9. (5) Payment of 3¼ days' wages during the period of strike.
Hua Yang Printers' Union, 8 Paoshan Road, Shanghai.
(1) Reinstatement of dismissed workers in Shun-li Printing Shop. (2) All demands be handed over to the Municipal Government of Greater Shanghai for arbitration.
Tobacconists and Money Exchangers, Nantao, Shanghai.
Shanghai Weaving Factory No. 1, 2218 East Yuhang Road, Shanghai.
Tang Yong Chi Silver Smith, Sing Kong Li, Tatung Road, Shanghai.
Say Lun Silk Filature, 25 Miller Road, Shanghai.
Yih Tien-teh Drug Store, 267 East Seward Road, Shanghai.
Ying Chong Match Factory No. 2, Loubado, Pootung.
Ta Shing Silk Filature, Ching Yung Road, Shanghai.
Yung Hsia Silk Weaving Factory, New Republic Road, Chapei, Shanghai.

table.title: Strikes in November, 1928
table.caption_extra: Shanghai Strikes in 1928 — The following is a summary of the strikes during November :*

rows: Foreign Style Tailoring Employees' Association, 3 Loh Hsing Li, Jukong Road, Shanghai.
Refusal on the part of the management to grant the workers' demands for better treatment and increases in wages.

(1) Recognition by the management of the representative right of employees' union. (2) $300 monthly allowance to be given by the management to the union. (3) No dismissal of the employees without a thorough investigation by the union. (4) No employment of non-members of the union. (5) Sundays and other commemoration days set as holidays by the National Government or other high official organs to be observed as such with full pay. (6) Double pay at the end of every year, and regular pay for the New Year Holidays from the 1st to the 5th of the 1st moon. (7) 8 hours of work per day, and 2-hour's pay for every one hour of night work. (8) Increases in wages : (a) $1.20 per coat and $0.90 per pair of trousers to be fixed as piece rate paid to hired labour by the management. (b) 30 per cent increase for regular employees earning over $10 per month, 20 per cent for over $20, and 10 per cent for over $30. (c) 75 per cent of the charges for contract labour sublet to hired employees by the management to belong to the employees and 25 per cent to the management. (d) )Boarding for regular employees to be supplied free by the management. (e) 30 per cent increase of minimum piece rate of $4 per winter suit, and $3 per spring coat or overcoat for contract labour. (f) 30 per cent increase of ordinary rate for a tuxedo or a morning coat. (g) 50 per cent increase of the ordinary rate for a frock coat. (h) 30 per cent increase of minimum rate of $2.80 for a summer suit (i) 30 per cent increase of the minimum rate of $1.80 for a white sailcloth suit. (j) A general 30 per cent increase of rate of charges for contract labour sublet to hired employees. (9) Apprenticeship : (a) The period of apprenticeship to be limited to 2 years. (b) The age of the apprentice to be not under 15. table.title: Strikes in December, 1928
table.caption_extra: Shanghai Strikes in 1928 — A summary for strikes in December follows* :—

rows: Shanghai Cotton Weaving Union Labour Association, 5 Shih Teh Lee, Yung Shin Road, Chapei.
French Tramway, Electric Lighting and Water Works Company.
1st strike on Dec. 3 : 2nd strike on Dec. 16.
1st strike ended Dec. 12 : 2nd strike ended Dec. 29.
Failure on the part of the management to accede to the request of the employees for better treatment.

1.—That the labour union be recognized, and be the sole organization entitled to represent the workers. 2.—That no workers be dismissed without reason, and that special commendation be awarded to the diligent workers. 3.—That all workers who have been dismissed since September 30 be reinstated, and that wages be issued to them for the period during which they were idle. 4.—That a flat increase of 30 per cent in wages be granted to all workers. 5.—That the working time be fixed at eight hours per day. 6.—That a gratuity on the following basis be granted to workers who resign : A sum equivalent to one year's wages be given to those who have completed five years' service or work. A sum equivalent to two years' wages be given to those who have conpleted ten years' service or work. A gratuity should be doubled in the cases of those who die of sickness while on duty. 7.—The all anniversaries and festivals be observed as holidays, and that double wages be issued to employees who are called upon to do work on these occasions. 8.—That all rules and conditions prepared by the Company in controlling work be sent to the Social Bureau of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai for perusal and approval. 9.—That all medical expenses of employees be defrayed by the company. 10.—That any worker who, in the execution of his duties, becomes an invalid be given a life compensation by the company. 11.—That a contribution of $5,000 be made by the company to the fundamental fund of the union, and a monthly contribution of $500 towards its unkeep aftewards. 12.—That double pay be issued on the occasion of the Chinese New Year. 13.—That those who serve on the standing committee of the union be given leave to apply for that pay. 14.—That an additional worker be put on every car to take charge of the opening of doors. 15.—That the promotion of workers be based upon seniority and rank. 16.—That when vacancies arise, preference be given to those who were formerly dismissed.

(1) Demands 1 and 2 are granted. Better treatment to be accorded those employees who are best behaved and most industrious. (2) Drivers and conductors are to receive 20 cents bonus every day, instead of 10 cents as previously provided. (3) An extra pay for two days to be made to those employees who work 25 days in a month. Employees, who work less than 25 days in a month, because of sickeness in the company's hospital receive 25 days' wages in full. (4) Tramcars with two doors at the ends to be conducted by two conductors. (5) Employees working more than the prescribed office hours to receive extra wages according to the amount of over-time taken. (6) For all Sundays and public holidays employees receive full pay, while those working on such days receive double pay. (This provision is being negotiated on.) (7) Drivers, brass-smiths and members on the mechanical staff receive an additional sum of two dollars, beside an official increase of 10 per cent of wages. (8) Annual bonus to be given according to the following regulations : (a) A bonus representing 50 per cent of a month's wage be given those having worked for a year. (b) A bonus representing one-third of a month's wages be given those having worked for six months. (c) A bonus representing 20 per cent of a month's wages be given those having worked for three months. (9) Employees who become sick while on duty, and because of it, to be paid full, while those who become sick for other reasons, when proved by doctors, receive half of their wages. (10) Employees who become maimed while on duty receive medical expenses, and special compensation. (11) An appropriation of $1,000 to be made by the company for establishing schools for employees' children, and a monthly subsidy of $200 for their maintenance. (12) Employees chosen delegates to the Tramway Labour Union to be exempted from duty, but no wage for such absence be given. They may return to the company after their terms of office expire. (13) Increase of wages of the employees to be made in accordance with seniority and term of employment.

(1) The dismissed employees be asked to return to the shop. (2) Wages of the dismissed employees during the strike be paid in full.
